meta.name: Taavod Cyan and Navy
meta.description: Reference-led learning and career workspace; approved animated clay portrait; user-selected cyan and navy.
source_references: User reference images 1–4: white pill and list interfaces
User reference image 5: soft finance dashboard

color.palette_type: cyan and navy with white and pale ice surfaces

neutral.usage: White work panels on pale gray; navy text and cyan accents

color.contrast_strategy: dark-on-light dominant; neutral depth with visible keyboard focus

typography.font_style_notes: Apple system sans on macOS; large plain headings, no decorative fonts

layout.grid_system: Responsive CSS grids with persistent desktop sidebar
layout.columns: 2 main columns on dashboard; 3 learning cards at wide widths
layout.alignment_tendency: strict grid with asymmetric dashboard emphasis

shape.divider_style: fine neutral lines where grouping needs them

elevation.depth_cues: raised pills, inset inputs, matte layered cards

iconography.style: simple rounded outline with selective pastel tiles

motion.philosophy: functional UI motion; expressive facial rig, reduced-motion static pose

components.button_style: raised white pill or charcoal primary pill
components.card_style: white rounded panels with faint shadows
components.navigation_pattern: ChatGPT-like sidebar, active raised row, mobile drawer
components.modal_style: rounded white dialog with soft broad shadow
components.list_style: airy rows with small icons and clear primary text
components.component_notes: shadcn/Radix primitives throughout; avoid colored borders around every card

aesthetic.visual_metaphor: a quiet personal workspace with a small helpful companion

visual_language.whitespace_usage: generous around headings and between work areas
visual_language.visual_weight_distribution: strong headline, light surfaces, small colorful indicators
visual_language.focal_strategy: one portrait-inspired companion and useful primary action
visual_language.contrast_level: high text contrast, subtle surface contrast
visual_language.texture_usage: matte clay character, clean UI surfaces

composition.flow_direction: sidebar to headline to weekly work
composition.grouping_strategy: related actions in distinct soft panels
composition.negative_space_role: reduce visual noise and preserve focus

imagery.photo_treatment: source portrait used only for character reference
imagery.illustration_style: Approved portrait-derived clay artwork, compact curls, side fade and short boxed beard
imagery.graphic_elements: small pastel icon tiles, narrow gradient accents

interaction_feel.feedback_style: clear state labels, gentle raised controls
interaction_feel.hover_behavior: small lift on buttons; direct gaze reaction

overview.fallback_strategy: Exact approved neutral portrait while loading, when reduced motion is active, or if graphics are unavailable
overview.primary_technology: PixiJS WebGL portrait layers; full Bloub state engine for animation

background_effects.description: Solid pearl workspace; static soft gradient on login

3d_elements.description: Superseded approximate mesh; approved clay portrait is rendered as a 2D facial rig.

shader_effects.description: Default Pixi textured rendering; no bespoke shader effects

cursor_effects.description: Native cursor; companion gaze follows pointer

image_effects.description: Feathered eyelid/mouth keyframes and localized pupil movement; approved haircut, beard and face silhouette preserved

params.reveal_animation: approved artwork shown immediately while renderer loads

canvas_drawings.description: Approved short-curl/fade portrait with independently composited eyelid and mouth keyframes; local pupil/brow mesh deformation

params.responsiveness: Responsive to companion container, resolution capped at 2
params.interaction: Bloub gaze interpolation, wink, expression transitions and thinking pulse

svg_animations.description: Bloub motion functions reused on 3D meshes instead of its SVG silhouette

visual_effects.composite_notes: Reference screenshots show static 3D/orb imagery and tactile UI. Runtime motion is an implementation choice informed by Bloub and the user request; never inferred as observed animation in still screenshots.
